title: ‘Plants get sick!’: WashU scientists, U. City students research plants together
summary_en: Biologist Rachel Penczykowski, in WashU Arts & Sciences, is an expert in infectious disease in plants. She conducts much of her research in the field — rural farmland, urban parks and, on this sunny day, a garden bed at Jackson Park Elementary School in the University City School District.
title_cn: ‘Plants get sick!’: WashU scientists, U. City students research plants together

title: What mice and crayfish can teach us about evolution
summary_en: By studying two very different animals, biologist Andreas Kautt in WashU Arts & Sciences is uncovering the genetic changes that help species adapt and diversify.
title_cn: What mice and crayfish can teach us about evolution

title: Global consortium launches AI tools to accelerate Alzheimer’s research, treatments
summary_en: The consortium co-founded by WashU Medicine, C-BRAIN, brings together members from academia, major pharmaceutical companies and philanthropic organizations.
title_cn: Global consortium launches AI tools to accelerate Alzheimer’s research, treatments

title: Dementia rising across Latino populations, multidecade study finds
summary_en: A two-decade study led by WashU Medicine neurologist Jorge Llibre-Guerra, MD, provides the first direct evidence based on door-to-door surveys of older adults that dementia is rising across several Latin American and Caribbean sites, even as rates hold steady or fall in wealthier nations.
title_cn: Dementia rising across Latino populations, multidecade study finds
